scope: Selected technical and lexical facts checked against primary sources. Teaching definitions, examples, translations and notes are original; no copied source passages or claim of certification of all48 cards.

references.title: Parameter
references.checked_fact: A function parameter is a named variable declared by the function; the argument is the actual value passed in a call. The reference supports the parameter/argument distinction, not an assertion that every function must return a value.

references.title: Overview of HTTP
references.checked_fact: In an HTTP exchange, the client sends a request and the server replies with a response. The response includes a status code indicating the outcome. A response need not mean success or contain the requested data.

references.title: 404 Not Found
references.checked_fact: 404 indicates that the requested resource was not found. It alone does not establish that the whole server has stopped or that the absence is permanent.

references.title: XMLHttpRequest: timeout property
references.checked_fact: A request can be terminated when its configured time limit is reached. The teaching note describes the time-limit result without assigning a particular cause or HTTP status.

references.title: input type=email
references.checked_fact: Email-format validation does not confirm that an address exists or is owned by the person entering it. Read-only relates to editing, not whether a resource is private. A read-only input can still be changed by script.

references.title: Pull requests
references.checked_fact: Pull requests propose code changes and provide a place to discuss or review them before merging. Opening a pull request does not itself mean its changes have been merged.

references.title: About issues
references.checked_fact: Issues can track bugs, ideas or tasks. The card uses one bug example without treating every issue as a bug.

references.title: Branches
references.checked_fact: Branches organize separate lines of work and are created from existing branches. A branch name does not by itself say that its content is private or accepted.

references.title: documentation noun
references.checked_fact: Documentation is uncountable in the software-instructions sense selected here. The word document can refer to one countable item.

references.title: permission
references.checked_fact: The general allowance sense is uncountable and supports permission to do something. The card separately explains plural permissions for individual system rights.

references.title: folder
references.checked_fact: The selected countable computer sense groups files.

references.title: export
references.checked_fact: The selected verb sense moves computer data into a different file or program. The separately cited US pronunciation page supplies a valid initial-stress verb form; no universal noun/verb stress rule is asserted.

references.title: resolve
references.checked_fact: The selected verb sense concerns solving a problem or disagreement, consistent with resolving a conflict.

references.title: timeout
references.checked_fact: The primary Business IT entry supports the one-word noun timeout for an operation exceeding its allowed duration. The card distinguishes that noun from the verb phrase time out.
